column1: # THE HONORIFIC REGISTER — Tournadre & Sangda Dorje, Manual of
# copy). The definitive taxonomy. Facts with citation; in-house.
#   spyir btang zhe sa   = general honorific (H)
#   zhe sa mtho po       = HIGH honorific (HH) — "especially high
#   dma' sa bzung ba'i zhe sa = humilific (h; term coined S. Beyer
#                          toward the person the action is directed to
#   phyogs gnyis kyi zhe sa = double honorific (hH) — subject AND
# KEY FACTS: honorific NEVER used of oneself (humilific instead);
# "only a FEW high and double honorifics, and they are not often
# used" (p.447); mixed registers in one sentence = zhe sa rkang chag
# "lame honorifics" (p.448); in LITERATURE the honorific plays a
# grammatical role — substitutes for person marking, identifies who
# HONORIFIC PREFIXES (~a dozen, p.448): sku(body) phyag(hand)
# gzim(sleep). [ljags CONFIRMS the Hackett ljags-klog reading.]
# sku's wide field (p.448): sku khrag(blood) sku stod(shirt)
# sku chas(possessions) sku brnyan(statue) sku mgron(guest)
# ADJECTIVES (few, p.449): skyid po/zhim po→spro po(H);
# mnyam du→lhan rgyas(H); mgyogs po→(H, rare); rare suffix
# "gnang ngo": 'jam po→'jam gnang ngo, dben po→dben gnang ngo
